title: Function-level structural diffs in diff_impact
description:
## Motivation

Sutra's `sutra_diff_impact` identifies which files changed and which symbols are affected (transitive callers), but it doesn't report *how* each symbol changed — was it added, deleted, modified, or did its signature change? This is the most valuable gap identified from surveying git-prism (`/home/josh/soft/sutra-surveys/git-prism`), which provides per-function change classification (added/modified/deleted/renamed/signature_changed) using tree-sitter and content-hash diffing.

## What this enables

- Review tools can surface "public API changed" vs "implementation-only change" distinctions
- Component-level summaries like "the public surface of this component shifted"
- Better risk scoring — signature changes are higher-risk than body-only changes
- Agents get structured change semantics instead of raw diffs

## Approach sketch

Compare the symbol table (name, kind, signature, signature_hash, start/end lines) between two refs. Sutra already stores `signature_hash` per symbol — diffing two snapshots could classify each symbol as added/deleted/signature_changed/body_changed. The tricky part is doing this without a second full parse: either parse both refs on demand, or compare current index state against `git show HEAD~1:file` parsed on the fly.

## Prior art

git-prism's `get_change_manifest` does this with tree-sitter for 13 languages, comparing function-level content hashes between two refs. Their approach is on-demand (no persistent index), ours would leverage the existing index for the current state and only parse the prior ref.
